rationale: Retain sparse measured features for both bottle picks: EEF location at reference closure, the closed command plateau, terminal upward displacement from closure, and a local terminal height usable without that earlier anchor. Bounds are recomputed per episode using the explicit operator priors; they are not calibrated grasp or physical feasibility regions. No required orientation, full-path position corridor, or inter-arm geometry is inferred.

rules.rationale: Localize each EEF at its recorded closing threshold crossing around a fixed measured world point. This is an operator-prior reference-location envelope, not an object contact point or a verified grasp region. Development v2 calibration: explicit fixed-reference physical tolerance; original activation, frame, penalty scale and weight retained. This allows variation, not proof of contact or success. V3 coarse exposed-development candidate; fixed reference activation and penalty scale preserved; no object-state labels.

Preserve the measured closed command during the subsequent bottle lift and terminal hold. Command fraction alone establishes neither finger distance nor force, contact, or retention. Development v2 calibration: explicit fixed-reference physical tolerance; original activation, frame, penalty scale and weight retained. This allows variation, not proof of contact or success.

Measure the terminal EEF rise along world positive Z relative to its first recorded closure. This endpoint constraint does not impose a monotone lift path or measure bottle clearance. The original closure anchor must be inside the training chunk. Development v2 calibration: explicit fixed-reference physical tolerance; original activation, frame, penalty scale and weight retained. This allows variation, not proof of contact or success.

Retain the demonstrated final EEF height as a local endpoint feature when the closure-to-terminal displacement is masked because its anchor is outside the chunk. Leave terminal horizontal position and orientation free; height alone does not prove bottle support or retention. Development v2 calibration: explicit fixed-reference physical tolerance; original activation, frame, penalty scale and weight retained. This allows variation, not proof of contact or success.

Require an open-command fraction on stable fully-open fixed-reference plateaus; allow explicit timing slack in fraction space. This cannot assert contact or physical finger aperture. Generated events never control activation. V3 coarse exposed-development candidate; fixed reference activation and penalty scale preserved; no object-state labels.

Reference-frame EEF axis relation with explicit angular freedom at reference closure or fixed closed plateaus. Rotation about this chosen local axis remains free. This is a grasp-direction hypothesis, not an observed contact normal.
Second nonparallel EEF localX axis at fixed first reference closure, with coarse angular freedom. Complements localY while avoiding full-trajectory orientation fitting; does not prove contact.

A single world-X coordinate interval centered on the fixed reference closure point, conjoined with existing radial/angle/TCP constraints. Task world frame and mechanical TCP provenance are explicit. No newwhole-pathXYZ box and no objects/native labels used by loss. Exposed-development hypothesis, not object-clearance proof.
